In digital circuit design, flip-flops are important building blocks that are used to store and manipulate binary data. In this problem, you are tasked with implementing a flip-flop using Verilog HDL. Specifically, you will implement a D flip-flop using a gated clock.

The D flip-flop has two inputs: D (data) and CLK (clock), and two outputs: Q (output) and Q_N (negated output). When the clock signal transitions from low to high (the rising edge), the value of D is transferred to Q and Q_N. Otherwise, the outputs remain unchanged.

You will implement the D flip-flop using the following module:

```
module d_ff_gated_clock (
    input D,
    input CLK,
    output Q,
    output Q_N
);
```

Your implementation should use the provided gated clock, which is a clock signal that is only active when a separate enable signal is also active. Specifically, the enable signal EN is active-high, and the clock signal CLK is only active when EN is high.

Your implementation should meet the following requirements:
- The flip-flop should be implemented using only combinational logic (i.e., no sequential logic).
- The flip-flop should be edge-triggered (i.e., it should only update the output on the rising edge of the clock).
- The flip-flop should use the provided gated clock, with the enable signal EN connected to a separate input pin.
original_rtl:
module d_ff_gated_clock (
    input D,
    input CLK,
    input EN,
    output Q,
    output Q_N
);

wire gated_clk = CLK & EN; // create gated clock signal

assign Q = gated_clk ? D : Q; // update Q on rising edge of gated clock
assign Q_N = gated_clk ? ~D : Q_N; // update Q_N on rising edge of gated clock

endmodule
